case_studies.title: Carolina Guide: A Multi-Agent RAG System with Institutional Guardrails for Academic Policy Assistance
case_studies.abstract: University students often struggle to navigate complex academic policies, leading to advising bottlenecks and delayed access to critical information. Although large language models (LLMs) offer promise for automated assistance, their tendency toward hallucination and inability to enforce institutional constraints make them unsuitable for high-stakes policy guidance without careful architectural design. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of navigating complex academic policies by building a retrieval-augmented generation system called Carolina Guide. The system uses a multi-agent pipeline to provide accurate and institutionally compliant policy guidance. The result is a system that can efficiently assist university students with academic policy inquiries.

case_studies.title: Text-Driven 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis in Non-Manhattan Environments
case_studies.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in 3D indoor synthesis for Manhattan environments. However, existing methods often fail to capture plausible object layout patterns in non-Manhattan settings, primarily because they struggle to model non-orthogonal spatial relationships, leading to high geometric violations and low physical fidelity. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of generating 3D indoor scenes in non-Manhattan environments, where existing methods often fail to capture plausible object layouts. The researchers built a novel text-driven framework called SPG-Layout to generate physically plausible indoor scenes. The result is a more realistic and accurate 3D scene synthesis in complex environments.
